sentences.cn_text: 音乐对不同的人意味着不同的东西，有时甚至对同一个人在其生命的不同时刻也意味着不同的东西。
sentences.en_text: Music means different things to different people and sometimes even different things to the same person at different moments of his life.

sentences.cn_text: 它可能是诗意的、哲学的、感性的或数学的,但无论如何,在我看来,它必须与人类的灵魂有某种关联。
sentences.en_text: It might be poetic, philosophical, sensual, or mathematical, but in any case it must, in my view, have something to do with the soul of the human being.

sentences.cn_text: 因此它是形而上的;但其表达手段却是纯粹且完全物理的:声音。
sentences.en_text: Hence it is metaphysical; but the means of expression is purely and exclusively physical: sound.

sentences.cn_text: 我相信,正是形而上信息通过物理手段传递的这种永久共存构成了音乐的力量所在。
sentences.en_text: I believe it is precisely this permanent coexistence of metaphysical message through physical means that is the strength of music.

sentences.cn_text: 这也是为什么当我们试图用语言描述音乐时,我们所能做的只是阐述我们对它的反应,而无法把握音乐本身。
sentences.en_text: It is also the reason why when we try to describe music with words, all we can do is articulate our reactions to it, and not grasp music itself.

sentences.cn_text: 贝多芬在音乐中的重要性主要体现在其作品的革命性特质。
sentences.en_text: Beethoven’s importance in music has been principally defined by the revolutionary nature of his compositions.

sentences.cn_text: 他将音乐从迄今为止盛行的和声与结构惯例中解放出来。
sentences.en_text: He freed music from hitherto prevailing conventions of harmony and structure.

sentences.cn_text: 有时我在他的晚期作品中感受到一种打破所有连续性迹象的意志。
sentences.en_text: Sometimes I feel in his late works a will to break all signs of continuity.

sentences.cn_text: 音乐是突兀的,似乎是断裂的,如同最后一首钢琴奏鸣曲那样。
sentences.en_text: The music is abrupt and seemingly disconnected, as in the last piano sonata.

sentences.cn_text: 在音乐表达上,他并未感到受传统重负的束缚。
sentences.en_text: In musical expression, he did not feel restrained by the weight of convention.

sentences.cn_text: 据各方说法,他是一个思想自由的人,也是一个勇敢的人,而我认为勇气是理解其作品的必要品质,更不用说演奏其作品了。
sentences.en_text: By all accounts he was a freethinking person, and a courageous one, and I find courage an essential quality for the understanding, let alone the performance, of his works.

sentences.cn_text: 事实上,这种勇敢的态度成为了贝多芬音乐演奏者的必备条件。
sentences.en_text: This courageous attitude in fact becomes a requirement for the performers of Beethoven’s music.

sentences.cn_text: 他的作品要求演奏者表现出勇气,例如在力度运用方面。
sentences.en_text: His compositions demand the performer to show courage, for example in the use of dynamics.

sentences.cn_text: 贝多芬以极强的力度增大音量,然后突然转入柔和乐段的习惯,在他之前的作曲家中极少被采用。
sentences.en_text: Beethoven’s habit of increasing the volume with an extreme intensity and then abruptly following it with a sudden soft passage was only rarely used by composers before him.

sentences.cn_text: 从广义上说,贝多芬是一个深具政治性的人。
sentences.en_text: Beethoven was a deeply political man in the broadest sense of the word.

sentences.cn_text: 他对日常政治不感兴趣,而是关注道德行为问题以及影响整个社会的是非大问题。
sentences.en_text: He was not interested in daily politics, but concerned with questions of moral behavior and the larger questions of right and wrong affecting the entire society.

sentences.cn_text: 尤为重要的是他对自由的看法,对他而言,自由与个人的权利和责任相关联:他主张思想自由和个人表达自由。
sentences.en_text: Especially significant was his view of freedom, which, for him, was associated with the rights and responsibilities of the individual: he advocated freedom of thought and of personal expression.

sentences.cn_text: 贝多芬的音乐倾向于从混乱走向秩序,仿佛秩序是人类存在的必然要求。
sentences.en_text: Beethoven’s music tends to move from chaos to order as if order were an imperative of human existence.

sentences.cn_text: 对他而言,秩序并非源于遗忘或忽视困扰我们生存的混乱;秩序是一种必要的发展,是一种可能通向希腊精神升华理想的改善。
sentences.en_text: For him, order does not result from forgetting or ignoring the disorders that plague our existence; order is a necessary development, an improvement that may lead to the Greek ideal of spiritual elevation.

sentences.cn_text: 「英雄交响曲」的葬礼进行曲不是最后乐章而是第二乐章,这并非偶然,这样痛苦就不会成为最终结论。
sentences.en_text: It is not by chance that the Funeral March is not the last movement of the Eroica Symphony, but the second, so that suffering does not have the last word.

sentences.cn_text: 人们可以这样解读贝多芬的许多作品:痛苦是不可避免的,但与之抗争的勇气使生活值得一过。
sentences.en_text: One could interpret much of the work of Beethoven by saying that suffering is inevitable, but the courage to fight it renders life worth living.
